## Executor.resolve() method

Resolve one reference into the record or records it denotes, in wire form shaped by `request.outputPlan`<!-- -->.

**Signature:**

```typescript
resolve(request: ResolutionRequest): Promise<WireValue>;
```

## Remarks

A single reference (cardinality `'one'`<!-- -->) resolves to the record. An identity reference whose id matches nothing, or a name selector with no match, fails with `TargetNotFoundError`<!-- -->. An index selector past the end of its container fails with `InvalidSelectionError`<!-- -->.

A collection reference (cardinality `'many'`<!-- -->) resolves to an array of records, possibly empty. A range selector that extends past the end of its container fails with `InvalidSelectionError`<!-- -->; failure is never turned into an empty result. An identity collection resolves its entries in order; when an entry's target no longer exists it fails with `TargetNotFoundError` whose `entryIndex` names that entry's zero-based position, and the entry is never silently dropped. An identity collection with no entries resolves to `[]`<!-- -->.

Container chains are evaluated natively, to locate the target, and contribute no data to the result.

Like `execute`<!-- -->, it receives no credential or authority: authorization has already happened.
